subject.title: fix(reef): bound legacy state file reads in doctor migration

question: For legacy Reef state that exceeds the new read caps, should Doctor stream/import it, stop safely pending recovery, or archive it and continue with partial runtime state?
rationale: The patch makes a user-data and upgrade-behavior choice that cannot be resolved from implementation mechanics alone: continuing after archival can leave canonical Reef state incomplete.

options.title: Stream legacy logs
options.body: Implement bounded streaming import for append-only audit and replay logs so the migration preserves existing state without a whole-file allocation.

options.title: Fail safely with recovery
options.body: Leave the source in place and make Doctor stop with a deterministic recovery command rather than completing a partial migration.

options.title: Accept partial migration
options.body: Keep archival-and-continue behavior only with explicit maintainer acceptance and user-facing recovery documentation.

recommendation.title: Stream legacy logs
recommendation.body: Implement bounded streaming import for append-only audit and replay logs so the migration preserves existing state without a whole-file allocation.

likelyOwner.reason: The current-head commit owns the extraction and control flow that determines oversized-file behavior.
